name: Second Wind
tagline: Energy, drive and mood for men over 45
about: Second Wind is a lifestyle-first guide for men who feel flat in midlife: an energy audit, a plain-English guide to testosterone testing, libido and performance factors you can change, and a 4-week plan to get your drive back.
persona: You are a men's health coach with a GP's caution: frank about sex, sleep and alcohol, sceptical of clinics selling testosterone, and clear that persistent symptoms deserve a proper check.

onboarding.title: Get your drive back
onboarding.subtitle: Honest answers give you a better plan.
bullets: Energy audit: sleep, drink, stress, movement
A 4-week plan to feel like yourself

profile.label: What's going on in life
profile.placeholder: new job, toddler at home, drinking most nights

tools.title: Energy audit
tools.subtitle: Where the energy is leaking
tools.prompt: Audit the profile's energy: sleep {sleep}, {drinks} drinks per week, exercise {move}, plus the life context in the profile. Sections: a table (Factor | Your status | Effect on energy, mood and testosterone | Fix), bullets ranking the three changes with the biggest likely payoff, steps for the first week, and a callout on symptoms that deserve blood tests rather than lifestyle tweaks (unexplained weight change, breathlessness, low mood lasting weeks).

tools.title: Should I get tested?
tools.subtitle: Testosterone, without the hype

inputs.label: Your symptoms
inputs.placeholder: no morning erections, tired, gym progress stalled, moody

tools.prompt: As general information, weigh whether these symptoms warrant a testosterone check: {symptoms}. Sections: text on what low testosterone does and does not typically cause and how often the same symptoms have other causes (sleep, alcohol, depression, thyroid, sleep apnoea), a kv of how testing works (morning sample, repeat test, what else is usually checked), bullets of questions to ask the doctor, and a callout warning about clinics that prescribe on a single test and the risks of treatment without proper assessment.

tools.title: Libido & performance
tools.subtitle: Lifestyle-first, no pills pushed
tools.prompt: For '{issue}' with pattern: {since}, give lifestyle-first general information. Sections: text on the most common causes in midlife men and what the pattern suggests (for example, intact morning erections usually point away from a physical cause), a table (Factor | How it affects this | What to change), steps for a 4-week plan, and a callout that erection problems can be an early sign of heart or blood-vessel disease and are worth a GP visit.

tools.title: 4-week second wind
tools.subtitle: Movement, sleep, drink, mood
tools.prompt: Write a 4-week plan for the profile's main complaint with {time} a day and '{kit}' equipment. Sections: a table (Week | Movement | Sleep rule | Alcohol rule | One mood habit), steps for a daily non-negotiable routine, a checklist of the weekly wins to tick, and a quote with one line to say to yourself on the flat days.

tools.title: Talk to my partner
tools.subtitle: Words for a hard conversation
tools.prompt: Write a {tone} conversation opener for talking to a partner about '{about}'. Sections: a quote with the opening two or three sentences, bullets of what to say if they react with worry, blame or relief, a kv of the asks (what you need from them, what you will do), and a callout on not having this conversation after drinking or in bed.

disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. Persistent tiredness, low mood or erection problems deserve a doctor's assessment; never start hormone treatment without proper testing and medical supervision.
